transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I'm here because I've been feeling extremely down, anxious, and overwhelmed lately. It has gotten to the point where it's really hard for me to cope with everything.
How long have you been feeling this down and anxious, and did it start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
It started about two months ago, right after I suddenly lost my job. Ever since then, I've been constantly worried about the future and just feeling really hopeless and down.
In the past two weeks, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep, appetite, or concentration. I'm not entirely sure about those, as I've mostly just been focused on the constant worry and feeling down.
Even with everything going on, are you still able to enjoy things you normally like, or have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities?
I'm not really sure if I've lost interest in those things. I've just been so overwhelmed by my situation that I haven't really thought about doing much of anything lately.
Before you lost your job, were you already someone who worried a lot about many different parts of life for at least six months, or did the anxiety mainly begin after losing the job?
No, I wasn't really a big worrier before this. This severe anxiety and constant worry only started after I lost my job, and I was doing fine before that happened.
Since losing your job, have these feelings been much stronger than you would expect for the situation and made it hard for you to manage daily responsibilities or relationships?

I'm not really sure if it's stronger than what's expected, but it certainly feels like too much to handle. It has definitely been really difficult to manage my daily routine and keep up with my family and friends lately.
In the past two weeks, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty, or had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
No, I haven't really felt worthless or had any thoughts like that. I'm just feeling incredibly sad and stressed about my job situation, but it hasn't gone that far.
During the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day for most of the day, or does it come and go depending on what’s happening?

I've definitely been feeling very sad and hopeless, but it isn't completely constant. It tends to come and go, and it gets a lot worse whenever I start thinking about losing my job or try to look for a new one.
When something distracting or positive happens, are you able to feel at least somewhat better for a while, or do you stay depressed no matter what?
I'm not quite sure and haven't really paid close attention to whether positive events temporarily lift my mood. I just know that I generally feel down or anxious most of the time.
Over the past two weeks, have you still been able to enjoy anything at all when you do it, like talking with family, watching something, or hobbies, or does almost nothing feel pleasurable anymore?
I'm not really sure if I still enjoy those things. Honestly, I haven't thought much about whether activities feel pleasurable lately because I've just been so overwhelmed by my situation.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Adjustment Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder], and based on this conversation they remain the same. Adjustment Disorder is still strongly supported because symptoms began within two months of a clear stressor (job loss), the anxiety/depressed mood is closely tied to that event, and there was no prior longstanding anxiety. Major Depressive Disorder remains possible because the patient reports significant sadness/hopelessness and impairment, but key depressive features are still unclear or not endorsed: no clear anhedonia, no clear neurovegetative changes, no worthlessness, no suicidality, and mood seems reactive to reminders of the stressor rather than persistently depressed most of the day nearly every day. More questioning is needed to distinguish stress-related adjustment symptoms from a full depressive episode.
